desc:
A country has n cities labelled 0 to n - 1. Each entry roads[i] = [a, b] is a two-way road between cities a and b.

The network rank of two different cities is the number of roads that touch at least one of them. A road that joins the two cities directly is counted only once. Return the largest network rank over all pairs of different cities.
constraints: No two roads join the same pair of cities
hints: Start with a single city: how many roads touch it?
For a pair of cities, adding their two degrees counts a direct road between them twice.
The rank of a pair is deg[i] + deg[j], minus one if i and j are joined by a road. With n at most 100 you can test every pair, using a set of edges for the direct-road check.
editorial: Compute the degree of every city and store the roads in a set of normalised pairs. For two different cities i and j, the roads touching either one number deg[i] + deg[j], except that a road directly between them was counted once for each end, so subtract one in that case. Trying all pairs takes O(n2) and n is only 100.

A faster idea sorts the cities by degree: only the cities with the largest and second largest degrees can matter, and ties need a little care because some pairs of top cities may be directly connected. That gets to O(n + m), but the quadratic scan is simpler and fully sufficient under these limits.
